question: A charge of $+1\ \mu$C is at the origin and $-1\ \mu$C is at $(0, 2\ \text{mm})$. The electric field at $(10\ \text{cm}, 0)$ is approximately \left(\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\ \text{N m}^2\text{C}^{-2}\right)
solution:
This is a short dipole ($p = 10^{-6} \times 2 \times 10^{-3} = 2 \times 10^{-9}$ C m) and the point is on its equatorial line at $r = 0.1$ m:
$$E = \frac{kp}{r^3} = \frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 2 \times 10^{-9}}{10^{-3}} = 1.8 \times 10^4\ \text{N/C}$$
